question: ABCD is a trapezium where BC || AD and AC = CD. If ∠ABC = 54° and ∠BAC = 60°, what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠ACD?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔABC, ∠BCA = 180° − (54° + 60°) = 66°.

Since BC || AD, alternate interior angle ∠CAD = ∠BCA = 66°.

In isosceles ΔACD (AC = CD), base angles are equal ⇒ ∠CDA = ∠CAD = 66°.

∴ ∠ACD = 180° − (66° + 66°) = 48°.

**∴ The correct answer is 48°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Trapezium ABCD where BC || AD.

∠ABC = 54°

∠BAC = 60°

AC = CD

**Calculation:**

⇒ In ΔABC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠BCA = 180° − (∠ABC + ∠BAC)

⇒ ∠BCA = 180° − (54° + 60°) = 180° − 114° = 66°

⇒ Since BC || AD, the alternate interior angles across transversal AC are equal.

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠BCA = 66°

⇒ In ΔACD, it is given that AC = CD.

⇒ In a triangle, angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

⇒ ∠CDA = ∠CAD = 66°

⇒ The sum of angles in ΔACD is 180°.

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − (∠CAD + ∠CDA)

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − (66° + 66°) = 180° − 132° = 48°

**∴ The correct answer is 48°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Trapezium

A convex quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides. The consecutive interior angles between the parallel sides always sum to 180°.

Isosceles Triangle Properties

If two sides of a triangle are equal in length, the angles opposite to them are also equal. The altitude dropped to the base also bisects the base.

Alternate Interior Angles Theorem

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the alternate interior angles formed on opposite sides of the transversal are perfectly equal.
